meta.description: Evidence-based exercise bank for longevity-optimized training. Each exercise carries internal metadata for workout generation. Sourced from WHO/ACSM guidelines, Attia Outlive framework, Galpin protocols, and meta-analytic evidence.

schema.name: Display name
schema.bucket: Primary weekly goal bucket(s) this exercise fills
schema.movement_pattern: squat | hinge | horizontal_push | vertical_push | horizontal_pull | vertical_pull | carry | rotation | locomotion | core_stabilization
schema.progression_chain: Array from beginner → advanced. Position of this exercise indicated by difficulty_tier

default_prescription.schedule_a: Heavy phase (months 1, 3) — lower reps, heavier load
default_prescription.schedule_b: Hypertrophy phase (months 2, 4) — higher reps, moderate load

schema.longevity_benchmarks: Which functional targets this exercise supports
schema.implicit_core: Boolean — does this exercise engage core as a stabilizer
schema.notes: Programming notes, cues, or safety considerations

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Entry point for squat pattern. Hold dumbbell/KB at chest. Focus on depth and upright torso. Teaches squat mechanics safely before barbell loading.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.notes: Foundation pattern. Use in warmups or for complete beginners. Focus on full depth, controlled tempo.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.notes: Primary lower-body strength builder. Target: 0.75×BW → 1.25×BW over 6-12 months. Requires solid goblet squat form first.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.notes: Demands more thoracic mobility and core bracing than back squat. Greater quad emphasis. Good variation for Build/Performance phases.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Teaches hip hinge pattern safely. Dumbbells allow natural hand position. Focus on hip push-back, slight knee bend, flat back.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Barbell allows heavier loading. Excellent hamstring and posterior chain developer.

exercises.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
exercises.notes: King of posterior chain lifts. Target: 1×BW → 1.5×BW over 6-12 months. Requires solid RDL form first. Higher spinal demand — form is critical.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.notes: Lower spinal stress than conventional. Great alternative for those with back concerns. Attia blueprint includes this on Friday full-body days.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.notes: Unilateral work corrects imbalances and trains balance. Research shows balance/coordination independently predict mortality (SRT data).

exercises.name: Bodyweight Lunge
exercises.notes: Starting point for unilateral lower work. Good warmup or beginner exercise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.notes: Highly functional — mimics stair climbing. Attia's Centenarian Decathlon includes stair climbing as a key task. Trains balance under load.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.notes: Isolation accessory for hamstrings. Supplements compound hinge work. Good for quad/hamstring balance.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.notes: Calves support ankle stability and walking economy. Important for fall prevention in later decades.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.notes: Maximal glute activation with low spinal stress. Good deadlift alternative for those with back concerns.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: More shoulder-friendly than barbell due to free range of motion. Good entry point before barbell bench.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Primary upper-push benchmark. Target: 0.5×BW → 1×BW over 6-12 months. Spotter or safety bars recommended.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.notes: Shifts emphasis to upper chest and front delt. Good variation for second push day of the week.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Harvard study: 40+ push-ups associated with 96% reduced CVD risk. Fundamental benchmark exercise. Track max reps quarterly.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Standing version demands more core stabilization. Seated version is easier entry point. Builds shoulder girdle strength for posture and function.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Back support reduces core demand. Good starting point to learn overhead pressing mechanics.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.notes: Target: 0.35×BW → 0.65×BW over 6-12 months. Standing barbell OHP is a full-body lift. Requires good shoulder mobility.

exercises.name: Dip (Parallel Bars)
exercises.notes: Excellent upper-body push compound. Use assisted machine or bands if bodyweight is too difficult initially.

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Pushdown
exercises.notes: Isolation accessory. Low priority — compound pushes cover triceps well. Include if time allows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row (Single Arm)
exercises.notes: Excellent beginner pull. Bench-supported version is very back-friendly. Unilateral work corrects imbalances. Builds grip incidentally.

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.notes: Heavy pulling compound. Requires good hip hinge position. Excellent for overall back thickness and posture.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.notes: Machine support reduces spinal load. Good alternative when fatigued or as a lighter variation.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Bodyweight horizontal pull. Adjustable difficulty by changing body angle. Great warmup or full-body day exercise.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.notes: Gold standard vertical pull. If unable to do full pull-ups, use band-assisted or lat pulldown. Builds grip and shoulder health simultaneously.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.notes: Bridge to unassisted pull-ups. Progressively use lighter bands. Track band thickness to measure progress.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Machine alternative to pull-ups. Adjustable weight makes it ideal for beginners. Good for lat development at higher rep ranges.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.notes: Critical for shoulder health and posture. Counterbalances pressing work. Should appear in nearly every upper-body session. Low joint stress makes it ideal for high frequency.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.notes: Low-priority isolation. Compound pulls cover biceps well. Include if time allows for elbow health and grip support.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.notes: Attia emphasizes carries for grip + whole-body stability. Target: 40% BW per hand. The PURE study makes grip strength a tier-1 longevity metric.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.notes: Attia gold standard: target 2 minutes. Also decompresses spine and improves shoulder health. Track max time quarterly.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.notes: Primary power exercise. Explosive hip extension trains fast-twitch fibers — the exact fibers aging destroys (Galpin). Attia includes on Friday sessions.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Plyometric power. Araújo 2025: muscle power outperforms strength as mortality predictor. Step down (don't jump down) to reduce joint impact. Start with low box.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Entry-level plyometric. No equipment needed. Land softly with bent knees. Develops explosive force production.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.notes: Full-body explosive movement. Requires slam ball (dead bounce). Great for power production and stress relief. Low injury risk.

exercises.name: Hang Power Clean
exercises.notes: High-skill Olympic lift variation. Maximum power output. Only introduce after several months of KB swings and deadlifts. Consider coaching.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike — Zone 2
exercises.notes: Attia's preferred Zone 2 modality for precise HR control. Target 113-132 bpm for 32yo. Conversational pace. Must be steady-state — no intensity spikes. Start at 30 min if untrained, add 5 min/week.

exercises.name: Rowing Ergometer — Zone 2
exercises.notes: Full-body low-impact Zone 2. Good rowing form is important — learn the leg-back-arms sequence. Slightly more upper body engagement than bike.

exercises.name: Brisk Walking — Zone 2
exercises.notes: Blue Zones data: daily walking is the universal centenarian exercise. May need incline to reach Zone 2 HR for fitter individuals. Outdoor preferred for sunlight/circadian benefit.

exercises.name: Easy Jog — Zone 2
exercises.notes: Higher impact than bike/row. Good bone density stimulus. Must maintain conversational pace — if breathing hard, slow down. Nasal breathing is a good intensity check.

exercises.name: Swimming — Zone 2
exercises.notes: Zero impact. Excellent for recovery-adjacent Zone 2. Requires competent swim technique to maintain steady effort. HR monitoring is harder in water.

exercises.name: VO2max Intervals — Bike (4×4)
exercises.notes: Norwegian 4×4 protocol: gold standard for VO2max. Helgerud 2007 showed 10-13% VO2max improvement in 8 weeks. Bike/rower safest for beginners (form doesn't degrade). Target ~169-179 bpm for 32yo during work intervals.

exercises.name: VO2max Intervals — Bike (3×3 Beginner)
exercises.notes: Scaled version for Foundation phase (weeks 1-4). Progress to 3×3.5 then 4×4 over 6-8 weeks. Add duration before adding intervals.

exercises.name: VO2max Intervals — Rower
exercises.notes: Rower VO2max alternative. Full-body engagement. Form must stay clean at high effort — watch for back rounding at end of intervals.

exercises.name: VO2max Intervals — Running
exercises.notes: Running intervals are effective but form degrades under fatigue. Higher injury risk than bike/rower. Best for those with running experience. Also provides bone density stimulus.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance
exercises.notes: BJSM 2022: inability to balance 10 sec on one leg predicted 84% higher all-cause mortality. Test and train. Progress to eyes closed.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance — Eyes Closed
exercises.notes: Benchmark target: 10+ seconds eyes closed. Significantly harder — removes visual balance input. Introduced in Building phase (weeks 5+).

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.notes: McGill Big 3 exercise. Anti-rotation and anti-extension under control. Appears in Attia's Monday and Friday warmups.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Foundation anti-extension exercise. Progress duration. Once 60 sec is easy, add complexity (arm/leg lifts, body saw) rather than just more time.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: McGill Big 3. Anti-lateral-flexion. Addresses oblique imbalances. Important for spine health under load.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.notes: Warmup spinal mobilization. Synchronize with breath. Appears in every Attia warmup sequence.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
exercises.notes: Hip internal and external rotation mobility. Important for squat depth and overall hip health. Getting on/off the floor is a key longevity skill.

exercises.name: Scapular CARs
exercises.notes: Controlled Articular Rotations for shoulder health. Appears in Wednesday upper-body warmup. Maintains shoulder joint range of motion.

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Rotation
exercises.notes: Thoracic mobility affects squat depth, overhead pressing, and posture. One of the areas that tightens most from desk work.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.notes: Okinawan centenarians get up/down from floor 30+ times daily. This hold develops the hip and ankle mobility for full-depth squatting. Hold onto a post for support if needed.

exercises.name: Toe Yoga
exercises.notes: Attia foundation exercise. Lift big toe independently, then other toes. Foot intrinsic strength supports balance and gait. Appears in Monday warmup.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.notes: Warmup activation for posterior shoulder. Counteracts pressing and desk posture. High frequency is beneficial.

exercises.name: Band Shoulder Dislocate
exercises.notes: Full shoulder ROM exercise. Use wide grip band or PVC pipe. Appears in Wednesday warmup. Progress by narrowing grip width.

exercises.name: Back Extension (GHD or Floor)
exercises.notes: Spinal erector endurance. Important for maintaining back health under compound lift loads. Controlled tempo — no momentum.

exercises.name: Rest Day Walk
exercises.notes: Active recovery. Outdoor, morning preferred for circadian benefit. Blue Zones universal practice. Must stay below RPE 3 — no training stimulus.

exercises.name: Foam Rolling (Full Body)
exercises.notes: Quads, hamstrings, lats, upper back, IT band. Aids muscle soreness and blood flow. Part of rest day protocol.

exercises.name: Static Stretching Routine
exercises.notes: Hip flexor, hamstring, pigeon pose, chest doorway stretch, lat stretch, calf stretch, thoracic extension over roller. Hold each 30-60 sec. Araújo 2024: low flexibility in men predicted 1.87× mortality.

zone2_cardio.label: Zone 2 Cardio
zone2_cardio.description: Steady-state at 60-70% max HR. Conversational pace.

vo2max_intervals.label: VO2max Intervals
vo2max_intervals.description: 4×4 Norwegian protocol or scaled version. 90-95% max HR.

strength_push.label: Strength: Push
strength_push.description: Horizontal + vertical pressing. Bench, OHP, push-ups, dips.

strength_pull.label: Strength: Pull
strength_pull.description: Rows + vertical pulls. DB rows, BB rows, pull-ups, pulldowns.

strength_lower.label: Strength: Lower
strength_lower.description: Squat + hinge patterns. Squats, deadlifts, lunges, step-ups.

power.label: Power
power.description: Explosive movements for Type II fiber preservation. KB swings, jumps, cleans.

stability_mobility.label: Stability & Mobility
stability_mobility.description: Balance, CARs, breathing, mobility drills. Baked into warmups + standalone.

rest_days.label: Rest Days
rest_days.description: Active recovery only. Walk 20-30 min + stretch/foam roll 10-15 min. Nothing above RPE 3.

exercises: zone2_bike OR zone2_row OR zone2_walk_brisk OR zone2_jog OR zone2_swim
zone2_bike OR zone2_row OR zone2_walk_brisk OR zone2_jog OR zone2_swim

vo2max.label: VO2max
vo2max.source: Attia: elite for a decade younger
vo2max.test_method: Wearable estimate, Cooper 12-min test, or lab

resting_hr.label: Resting Heart Rate
resting_hr.source: Above 75 bpm doubles CV risk vs below 60

grip_strength.label: Grip Strength
grip_strength.source: PURE study: each 5 kg decrease = 16% mortality increase

phase_1_foundation.focus: Movement quality, light loads, habit building
phase_1_foundation.zone2_start: 30 min if untrained, build to 45 min by week 4
phase_1_foundation.stability: Basics: eyes-open balance, bird dogs, cat-cow
phase_1_foundation.progression_rule: Add weight only when form is solid. 2-for-2 rule.

phase_2_building.focus: Heavier loads, add 4th set to main lifts
phase_2_building.deload: Week 6 — same exercises at 70% working weight, Zone 2 reduced 25%, skip VO2max

phase_3_performance.focus: See how much stronger you've become
phase_3_performance.targets: Farmer carries 40% BW/hand, dead hang 60+ sec
phase_3_performance.deload: Week 12 — full rest week. Walking only, daily stretching, progress assessment
